title: Jordan: King Hussein's family, Irbid and Jerash
summary: The band played two concerts in Jordan, a make-up date in Irbid after Benny Carter fell ill, and visited Jerash.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you meet Hussein, King Hussein?
He was over here at the time.
Oh, that's too bad.
But he's a great jazz fan.
That's what I heard.
In fact, they are the ones that sponsored the concert in Jordan, yeah, his wife, and the concert -- we had to do two concerts, it was so crowded in both of them. Just absolutely
You didn't play in that Roman amphitheatre, did you?
No.
That's where Duke played. They played in the old Roman amphitheatre.
No, we didn't play there. But we visited there. They still have shows in there.
Yeah, that's right.
Then we took a trip to a place called -- they had never heard jazz before in their life -- a place called Irbid. That's right outside of Jordan.
Yeah.
No, right outside of Damascus, we went to Damascus, a place called Irbid, and they were more curious than anything else.
How do you spell that?
I-r-b-i-d.
Oh, I don't know that.
Yeah, well, it's a small place. Well, it
was a make-up date because we weren't supposed to play there, but we missed a couple of dates by Benny Carter being sick, so we added this one in. And --
What sort of -- what was Benny's trouble?
Well, you know, the food over there, if you're not particular -- then you can be particular what you eat and still have, you know, the diarrhea.
You get it from --
Water, anything.
-- the water they wash the salad with.
Sometimes just breathing the air.
Yeah, sure, sure.

Very filthy over there. It's awfully filthy. But we went through a little city called Jerash (PHONETIC) and that's where Jesus walked during some of his younger days and it was just such a thrill. We had dinner there in a restaurant. Such a thrill to walk, you know, fantastic feeling, you know.
Yeah.
There was a little area there, the marketplace, still in existence, you know, the Roman columns and everything, where he used to shop, you know.
